=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:_poller_rb_judge_sandbox_attempt (lines 106-220), called from poller_judge_isolated (line 284) | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The combined review-blocked judge Codex fallback path fails to produce a verdict. CI test `test_combined_rb_judge_uses_verified_engine_and_its_worktree` fails for both `["ai:orchestrator-managed","ai:codex"]` and `["ai:done"]` parametrizations: `verdict.txt` is empty instead of containing `"opencode verdict\n"`. The claude path passes, so the regression is specific to the codex engine path in combined mode (RB_COMBINED_MODE=true with rb_access=write). The sandbox prepare-ephemeral succeeds (test assertion at line 247 passes), but the verdict is empty, indicating either `write_opencode_config.sh` fails (returning 77 and clearing output at line 294) or the sandbox `run` call fails. This was introduced by the merge commit which changed 924 lines in this script.
  WHY: The combined rb_judge codex path returns non-zero from `_poller_rb_judge_sandbox_attempt`, causing `poller_judge_isolated` to clear the output file at line 294 (`[ "${rb_rc}" -eq 0 ] || : > "${output_file}"`). The review-blocked judge then has no verdict, blocking PR resolution.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:extract_latest_valid_orchestrator_state (lines 3205-3240), identity check at lines 3221-3226, skip logic at lines 19492-19494 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: CI test `test_state_identity_failure_skips_reconstruction_and_state_writes` fails in orchestrate-poll shard 3. The test verifies that when `gh api user` fails (identity unavailable), state reconstruction and state writes are skipped. The merge commit modified 924 lines in this script, introducing a regression in the identity failure handling path. The test expects: (1) `ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_AUTHOR_FILTER ... outcome=identity_unavailable` in stderr, (2) "skipping this tracking issue and state reconstruction" in stdout, (3) no `search/issues` API calls, (4) only 1 comment on the tracking issue. One or more of these assertions now fail.
  WHY: If identity failure no longer skips reconstruction, the poller may proceed to reconstruct state and write comments using untrusted state data when the pipeline's own identity cannot be verified, violating the security invariant that only the authenticated pipeline account's state comments are trusted.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
